reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is instructional, demonstrating YouTube Help, feedback, and support-navigation procedures, including eligibility for direct partner email access. Its requests to view related tutorials, download a free traffic report, and subscribe are described as ordinary audience or channel promotion, with no connection to payment, credential disclosure, investment returns, or deceptive outcomes.

citations.quote: I'll actually go one step beyond that and actually show you how.
you can go down to the bottom and click on Help.
Now, if you go through here, you'll notice that you have the Contact Us option on the top.
click on the link to my free video traffic review right here

opening.argument: Judge, the video pairs a promised free resource with a specific action: viewers are told to click a link for a video traffic report said to help them get keywords, subscribers and viewers. The description supplies a destination outside YouTube for that report. That promise-and-click sequence matters because the viewer arrives for help contacting YouTube but is also directed toward the speaker's own offer. The record does not establish what happens after the click; that uncertainty should not erase the solicitation visible in the video.

citations.quote: make sure to click on the link to my free video traffic review right here, which will help you get those keywords, to get those subscribers and viewers to your YouTube channel and videos.
If you haven't done so already, click on the link here and download your free copy of the free Video Traffic Report: http://www.davidwalshonline.com/free-report/?vid=ver-delchan
I'll actually go one step beyond that and actually show you how.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The Help and Contact Us walkthrough is real, but it does not account for the later request to leave for the speaker's free report. Nor does calling that request ordinary promotion resolve the concern: the report is tied to a claimed benefit for the viewer, and the description gives a direct download link. Absence of a stated payment or credential request limits what can be alleged about the destination, but it does not make the click solicitation disappear.

citations.quote: you can go down to the bottom and click on Help.
which will help you get those keywords, to get those subscribers and viewers to your YouTube channel and videos.
click on the link here and download your free copy of the free Video Traffic Report: http://www.davidwalshonline.com/free-report/?vid=ver-delchan

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted report offer establishes a free download and a promotional claim about improving channel traffic, not an illicit reward or deceptive claim flow. The substantive walkthrough directs viewers to YouTube's own Help interface and explains a limit on direct email support. Nothing cited shows a required registration, payment, credential handoff or misrepresentation about receiving the report.

citations.quote: you can go down to the bottom and click on Help.
if you don't have those 75,000 hours or 4.5 million minutes view time on your channel you'll still go through the normal channels that everyone else goes through.
download your free copy of the free Video Traffic Report

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. A video presented as guidance on contacting YouTube ends with a free report offer, a link to obtain it, and a direct call to click. The speaker also describes the report as helping viewers gain keywords, subscribers and views. None of those elements alone proves a harmful destination. Together, though, they warrant scrutiny: a viewer seeking support is moved from a demonstrated help procedure toward an off-platform resource marketed with an easy-to-obtain benefit. The record shows the invitation, not what the linked page ultimately requires.

citations.quote: YouTube Support - How To Contact YouTube
If you haven't done so already, click on the link here and download your free copy of the free Video Traffic Report: http://www.davidwalshonline.com/free-report/?vid=ver-delchan
which will help you get those keywords, to get those subscribers and viewers to your YouTube channel and videos.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited Help, Contact Us and feedback material confirms that the tutorial contains genuine instructions. It does not explain away the separate free-report pitch. Showing how to send feedback is compatible with using the same video to draw viewers to another site. The defense is right that the record shows no payment or credential demand; the narrower concern is the combination of a free benefit claim and an explicit external-link call.

citations.quote: you'll notice that you have the Contact Us option on the top.
click on the link here and download your free copy of the free Video Traffic Report: http://www.davidwalshonline.com/free-report/?vid=ver-delchan

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The combined signals still support an ordinary tutorial with an appended channel promotion. The video demonstrates YouTube Help and feedback, and it explains that most viewers must use normal support channels. The free report is described as a resource for improving a channel; neither the offer nor the final click graphic establishes a deceptive acquisition process. Suspicion about an unseen destination cannot substitute for evidence of one.

citations.quote: you can go down to the bottom and click on Help.
you'll still go through the normal channels that everyone else goes through.
make sure to click on the link to my free video traffic review right here

opening.argument: Judge, look at where the instruction leads. The speaker demonstrates support navigation, then pivots to his goal of helping viewers build subscribers and views. He directs them to his video series and to a free report, while the description identifies his video-marketing work and provides the report link. This is not merely an incidental sign-off: the support lesson gives the speaker an audience to whom he can promote an easy-to-obtain resource. I would weigh that promotional function alongside the tutorial, rather than treating the tutorial as the whole purpose of the video.

citations.quote: my goal for this channel is that you have the best YouTube channel that you have but that you've also got thousands of subscribers and thousands and thousands of views on your YouTube videos.
If you want to get more viewers and subscribers, then click on the link right here, and click through to that video series.
make sure to click on the link to my free video traffic review right here
David Walsh is an expert in video marketing, information marketing, high end membership site creation and product launches.
To get your FREE Video Traffic Report go to: http://www.davidwalshonline.com/free-report

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to real support instructions, including Help and Contact Us. The issue is whether those instructions exhaust the video's function. They do not: the speaker expressly shifts to growing an audience, sends viewers to more videos, and offers a linked report. The defense calls those requests ordinary promotion, but that characterization leaves the promised free resource and requested click largely unanalyzed. The tutorial and the promotional funnel can coexist.

citations.quote: you can go down to the bottom and click on Help.
Now, if you go through here, you'll notice that you have the Contact Us option on the top.
If you want to get more viewers and subscribers, then click on the link right here, and click through to that video series.
To get your FREE Video Traffic Report go to: http://www.davidwalshonline.com/free-report

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is evident, but promotion is not enough. The central walkthrough gives concrete steps for Help, feedback and Contact Us, then explains why direct email support is unavailable to many users. The later requests concern related tutorials, a free traffic report and subscriptions. The prosecution's quotes show no misleading condition attached to the report and no evidence that clicking it yields anything other than the advertised resource.
